stemBlocks.value: (a)(i) Find the matrix product of the 2x2 matrix (-1  3 / 4  h) with the column matrix (k / 5). (ii) Hence find the values of h and k for which (-1  3 / 4  h)(k / 5) = (0 / 0). (b) Using a matrix method, solve the simultaneous equations 2x + 3y = 5 and -5x + y = 13.
Think first: Multiply out first and leave the answer in terms of h and k; the zero matrix then turns each entry into an equation.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p290-q01 from workbook page 290.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply each row of the 2x2 matrix by the column matrix.
Set the product equal to the zero column matrix and equate entries.

contentBlocks.value: Result: Two equations in h and k

solutionSteps.instruction: Solve for k, then substitute to find h.
For (b), write the equations as AX = B and find the determinant of A.
Write the inverse of A and use X = A inverse times B.

contentBlocks.value: Result: X = (-2 / 3), so x = -2 and y = 3

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply row by column to get the product in terms of h and k, set each entry to zero and solve, then write the simultaneous equations as AX = B and use X = A inverse times B.

whyThisWorks.value: Each entry of a matrix product is the sum of products of a row of the first matrix with the column of the second, so setting a product equal to the zero matrix gives one ordinary equation per entry. For simultaneous equations, writing them as AX = B lets you undo the multiplication by A: multiplying both sides on the left by A inverse leaves X on its own, and the inverse exists exactly when the determinant is not zero.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying corresponding entries instead of rows by columns.

commonErrors.misconception: Swapping the entries of the adjugate: the leading diagonal entries swap and the other two change sign, not the other way round.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying B by A inverse on the wrong side; matrix multiplication is not commutative.

examTip.value: Always check a matrix solution by substituting x and y back into both original equations; it takes ten seconds and catches sign slips in the inverse.
